content:
Most businesses in Gurugram already use WhatsApp every day. A clinic on Sohna Road confirms appointments on it, a coaching centre sends batch timings, and a showroom on MG Road shares product photos with walk-in customers. The problem is that most of this runs from one staff phone on the regular WhatsApp Business app. Chats get lost when that person is on leave, and broadcasts only reach people who saved your number.

Our WhatsApp marketing work moves you from that setup to the official WhatsApp Business Platform (often called the WhatsApp API). We are TopWebExpert, based in Sector 49 on Sohna Road, and this page explains what the service involves, what it needs from you, and when it is not worth doing.

App vs. API: which one do you actually need?

Not every business needs the API. The free WhatsApp Business app is fine if you handle a few dozen chats a day and one or two people reply to them. The platform makes sense when any of these is true:

  • More than one person needs to reply from the same business number, such as a sales team or front desk staff working in shifts.
  • You want to send updates to hundreds or thousands of customers who have opted in, not just to people who saved your contact.
  • Leads from your website, Google Ads or Meta ads should get an instant WhatsApp reply, and should be logged in your CRM.
  • You need order, booking or payment reminders to go out automatically.

If none of these apply yet, we will tell you to stay on the app and set it up well (catalogue, quick replies, labels, away messages). That takes an afternoon.

How the setup works, step by step

A typical setup takes one to three weeks. Most of it is waiting on verification and template approvals.

  1. Number decision. We check whether your chosen number is already on the WhatsApp app and what your provider supports. Some businesses move the number fully to the platform; others take a fresh number for it.
  2. Meta Business verification. Your business is verified in Meta Business Manager using documents such as GST registration or a certificate of incorporation, and a website on a matching domain. Mismatched details are the usual cause of delays.
  3. Provider and inbox. You connect either directly through Meta's Cloud API or through a Business Solution Provider that adds a shared team inbox, chatbot builder and campaign tools. We compare options against your volume and budget.
  4. Display name. Meta reviews your display name, which should match your brand on your website and signage.
  5. Opt-in collection. We add clear opt-in points: a checkbox on website forms, a line on Meta lead forms, a QR code at your reception or store counter, and a click-to-WhatsApp button on ads.
  6. Template writing and approval. Every message you start (outside a customer's 24-hour reply window) must use a template approved by Meta. We write and submit these, usually a first batch of five to ten.
  7. Automation and CRM link. Welcome replies, FAQ menus, and routing to the right team member are built, and new chats are pushed to your CRM or a Google Sheet.

Rules that decide whether your number survives

WhatsApp numbers get restricted or blocked when too many recipients block or report them. Meta tracks this as a quality rating, and a low rating limits how many people you can message per day. These rules protect that rating:

  • Only message people who opted in. Blasting a purchased list of Gurugram phone numbers is the fastest way to lose a number, and we don't do it.
  • Use the right template category. Meta classifies templates as marketing, utility or authentication, and charges differently for each. An order update can be utility; an offer is marketing. Mislabelled templates get re-categorised or rejected.
  • Respect the 24-hour window. When a customer messages you, you can reply freely for 24 hours. After that, only templates can be sent.
  • Give an easy way out. Every marketing template includes a simple opt-out, and opt-outs are honoured immediately.

Meta sets message charges by category and country and revises them from time to time, so we always check the current rate card before planning a campaign budget. These charges are paid to Meta or your provider, separately from our fee.

What happens every month

  • Planning two to four broadcast campaigns with you, based on what you actually have to say: new stock, a seasonal offer, a site visit weekend, a webinar.
  • Splitting your contact list by interest or stage (new enquiry, past customer, inactive) so each group gets relevant messages.
  • Writing and getting approval for new templates as needed.
  • Checking chatbot conversations for questions it fails to answer and fixing the flows.
  • Watching the quality rating and pausing any campaign that triggers a spike in blocks.
  • A monthly report and a short call to decide what to change.

What we need from you

We need business documents for verification, a person who owns the Meta Business Manager account (it should stay in your name, not ours), agreed answers to your common customer questions, and someone on your team who will reply to chats that the bot hands over. That matters most: if a hot lead writes back at 11 am and nobody answers until evening, the automation has not helped.

How we judge whether it is working

We report on numbers that come straight from the platform and your CRM, not vanity counts:

  • Delivery rate
  • Read rate
  • Reply rate
  • Block and opt-out rate
  • First response time
  • Leads or bookings per campaign
  • Cost per conversation or lead

A campaign with a high read rate but no replies usually means the message had no clear next step. A rising block rate means the audience or frequency is wrong.

When WhatsApp is the wrong channel

WhatsApp marketing is not a good fit if you have no opted-in customers and no plan to collect them, if nobody on your team can answer chats during working hours, or if your product needs long, formal documentation that suits email better. It also suits nobody who wants to send the same promotion to everyone every few days; that annoys recipients and damages the number.

Frequently asked questions

Can I keep using my existing WhatsApp number?

Usually yes. Depending on your provider, the number is either moved to the platform or, where Meta supports it, used on both the Business app and the platform. We confirm the options, including what happens to chat history, before anything is changed.

Is sending bulk WhatsApp messages legal?

Sending to people who have agreed to hear from you, through the official platform with approved templates, is how WhatsApp is meant to be used for business. Unofficial bulk-sending software breaks WhatsApp's terms, and numbers used that way often get banned.

How much does it cost?

There are three parts: Meta's per-message charges, any provider or inbox subscription, and our setup and management fee. Our fee depends on how many templates, flows and integrations you need and how many campaigns run each month. We give a fixed quote after a free consultation.

Can the chatbot answer in Hindi?

Yes. Templates and bot replies can be written in Hindi, English or both. Many customers in Gurgaon write in Hinglish, so we keep the language simple.

How soon can we send our first campaign?

If your business documents are in order, the first approved templates and a small campaign to existing opted-in customers can usually go out within two to three weeks of starting.
